scope.statement: Azure public-cloud IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, routing, transit, isolation, IP-boundary protection, and Layer 3 diagnostics exposed through documented management-plane state.
scope.responsibility_boundary: Customers configure address spaces, routes, peerings, gateways, public IP boundaries, and supported diagnostics. Microsoft owns and operates the physical fabric, tenant isolation, system-route implementation, packet forwarding, and other internals not exposed as tenant-verifiable state.

subdomains.name: Addressing and packet behavior
subdomains.description: IP addressing, prefix allocation, subnetting, NAT, public/private boundaries, fragmentation, MTU, ICMP, and source validation.

subdomains.name: Routing and forwarding
subdomains.description: Packet forwarding, next-hop selection, system and user-defined routes, propagation, effective routes, BGP, redundancy, and failover.

subdomains.name: Network transit
subdomains.description: Virtual network peering, hub-and-spoke topology, VPN Gateway, and ExpressRoute routing and advertisement.

subdomains.name: Protection and isolation
subdomains.description: DDoS protection, tenant boundaries, segmentation, and network isolation.

subdomains.name: Layer 3 observability
subdomains.description: Route diagnostics, flow visibility, reachability diagnostics, and monitoring coverage.

controls.title: IPv4 addressing and prefix management assurance
Virtual network peering and transit assurance
Public and private IP boundary assurance
IP fragmentation, MTU, and path MTU assurance
DDoS protection at the IP boundary assurance
Layer 3 monitoring and route diagnostics assurance

domains.name: IPv4 addressing and prefix management
domains.observability_method: Inspect VNet, subnet, NIC, and public IP management-plane configuration.
domains.automation_decision: Existing public-IP association check covers one boundary condition; broad prefix policy is deployment-specific.

domains.name: IPv6 addressing and dual-stack behavior
domains.observability_method: Inspect IPv6 VNet prefixes, subnet prefixes, NIC configurations, and public IP SKUs.
domains.automation_decision: No universal requirement to enable dual stack; absence is not a safe finding.

domains.name: Subnetting and address-space overlap
domains.observability_method: Compare authoritative VNet, subnet, peering, and connected-network prefixes.
domains.automation_decision: Azure prevents invalid local subnet overlap, while intended cross-network overlap requires topology context not currently inventoried.

domains.name: Packet forwarding and next-hop selection
domains.observability_method: Use Network Watcher next-hop diagnostics for a selected VM NIC and destination.
domains.automation_decision: NIC IP forwarding is checked from authoritative configuration; path-specific next-hop intent remains manual.

domains.name: System routes and user-defined routes
domains.observability_method: Inspect route tables and documented Azure system routes.
domains.automation_decision: Explicit user-defined default Internet routes are checked; system routes and intended private routing remain contextual.

domains.name: Route propagation and effective routes
domains.observability_method: Inspect route-table propagation settings and Network Watcher effective routes for selected NICs.
domains.automation_decision: Effective-route evaluation requires workload intent and NIC scope.

domains.name: Virtual network peering and transit
domains.observability_method: Inspect both peering directions, forwarded-traffic, remote-gateway, and gateway-transit flags.
domains.automation_decision: Existing peering transit rule supplies a limited management-plane check; full topology validity remains manual.

domains.name: Hub-and-spoke routing
domains.observability_method: Correlate peerings, route tables, gateways, and network virtual appliances against the intended topology.
domains.automation_decision: Inventory does not identify intended hubs, spokes, or routing functions, so topology assumptions cannot create findings.

domains.name: Network address translation
domains.observability_method: Inspect NAT Gateway attachment, outbound rules, and Azure-managed translation behavior.
domains.automation_decision: NAT design is workload-specific; public IP association is the only existing related check.

domains.name: Public and private IP boundaries
domains.observability_method: Inspect public IP resources and associations plus private subnet and NIC addressing.
domains.automation_decision: Existing rules check unused public IPs and selected segmentation boundaries; they do not prove end-to-end exposure.

domains.name: IP fragmentation, MTU, and path MTU behavior
domains.observability_method: Validate workload paths with documented Azure MTU guidance and controlled diagnostics.
domains.automation_decision: Management-plane inventory cannot prove packet fragmentation or path MTU behavior.

domains.name: ICMP and diagnostic reachability
domains.observability_method: Use Network Watcher connection troubleshoot and IP flow verification for an explicitly selected path.
domains.automation_decision: Reachability is path- and policy-specific; scanner inventory alone is insufficient.

domains.name: Source-address validation and anti-spoofing
domains.observability_method: Rely on Microsoft platform documentation; tenant inventory cannot inspect fabric enforcement.
domains.automation_decision: No customer-actionable authoritative state exists; no finding is safe.

domains.name: BGP routing
domains.observability_method: Inspect gateway BGP configuration and learned or advertised routes for an applicable gateway.
domains.automation_decision: BGP correctness depends on intended on-premises prefixes and policy.

domains.name: VPN gateway routing
domains.observability_method: Inspect VPN gateway, connection, local network gateway, routing, and effective route state.
domains.automation_decision: Existing VPN rule checks IKE configuration; route correctness remains contextual.

domains.name: ExpressRoute routing and route advertisement
domains.observability_method: Inspect circuit, gateway, peering, BGP, and advertised-route management-plane state when ExpressRoute is deployed.
domains.automation_decision: The MACsec rules are Layer 2 and deliberately excluded; Layer 3 advertisement correctness requires customer route intent.

domains.name: Route redundancy and failover
domains.observability_method: Inspect gateway redundancy mode and validate planned failover using service-specific diagnostics.
domains.automation_decision: Backend presence and VPN configuration are related cross-layer signals, not proof of route failover.

domains.name: DDoS protection at the IP boundary
domains.observability_method: Inspect VNet DDoS plan association and Microsoft platform protection documentation.
domains.automation_decision: Existing VNet DDoS rule checks authoritative plan association.

domains.name: Network isolation and segmentation
domains.observability_method: Inspect prefixes, subnets, peerings, route boundaries, NSGs, and firewall placement against architecture intent.
domains.automation_decision: Existing cross-layer rules provide limited configuration checks; platform tenant isolation is provider-owned.

domains.name: Layer 3 monitoring, flow visibility, and route diagnostics
domains.observability_method: Inspect Network Watcher availability and supported flow and route diagnostic configuration.
domains.automation_decision: Existing rules check selected diagnostic services; they do not constitute live traffic or fabric inspection.

rule_classifications.name: ExpressRoute Direct link without MACsec
rule_classifications.classification_basis: MACsec protects Ethernet frames on the direct link and remains a Data Link control.

rule_classifications.name: ExpressRoute Direct non-XPN MACsec cipher
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The MACsec cipher suite protects Ethernet frames and remains a Data Link control.

rule_classifications.name: Unrestricted inbound SSH
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The finding is selected by TCP destination port 22.

rule_classifications.name: Unrestricted inbound RDP
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The finding is selected by TCP destination port 3389.

rule_classifications.name: Unrestricted inbound HTTPS
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The finding is selected by TCP destination port 443.

rule_classifications.name: NSG with no rules
rule_classifications.classification_basis: NSGs evaluate Layer 3 prefixes and Layer 4 protocol and port tuples.

rule_classifications.name: VNet without DDoS plan
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The control protects the VNet IP boundary against network-layer denial of service.

rule_classifications.name: Unassociated public IP
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The resource represents an IP address and public/private boundary.

rule_classifications.name: Application Gateway without WAF
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Application Gateway WAF inspects HTTP application traffic.

rule_classifications.name: Load balancer without backend pool
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Azure Load Balancer spans IP frontend selection and transport-layer load balancing.

rule_classifications.name: VPN gateway using IKEv1
rule_classifications.classification_basis: IKE establishes the VPN security association while the gateway carries routed IP traffic.

rule_classifications.name: Subnet without NSG
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The subnet is Layer 3 while NSG policy can match Layer 3 and Layer 4 fields.

rule_classifications.name: Network Watcher regional coverage
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Network Watcher exposes Layer 3 route and reachability diagnostics plus broader network tooling.

rule_classifications.name: NSG flow logs disabled
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Flow records contain Layer 3 addresses and Layer 4 protocol and port information.

rule_classifications.name: VNet without Azure Firewall
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Firewall placement creates a Layer 3 boundary while policy can enforce through Layer 7.

rule_classifications.name: Peering gateway transit restrictions
rule_classifications.classification_basis: VNet peering and gateway transit determine routed IP reachability.

rule_classifications.name: Public DNS exposing private infrastructure
rule_classifications.classification_basis: DNS is an application-layer naming protocol even when records contain IP addresses.

rule_classifications.name: Network interface with IP forwarding enabled
rule_classifications.classification_basis: IP forwarding changes Layer 3 source, destination, and transit behavior on the network interface.

rule_classifications.name: User-defined default route using direct Internet next hop
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The route explicitly selects the Layer 3 next hop for all IPv4 or IPv6 destinations.

rule_classifications.name: Private Endpoint target retaining public access
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The control evaluates whether a PaaS resource retains a public IP network path alongside its private endpoint path.

rule_classifications.name: Private Endpoint connection not approved
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Private Endpoint connection state determines whether the target has an operational private IP network path.

rule_classifications.name: Private Endpoint missing Private DNS zone association
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The finding evaluates DNS naming configuration even though the resulting record identifies a private IP address.

rule_classifications.name: Private Endpoint DNS configuration reports only public addresses
rule_classifications.classification_basis: DNS is an application-layer naming protocol; this rule evaluates ARM custom DNS configuration and does not claim effective resolver-path evidence.

rule_classifications.name: Critical PaaS resource publicly accessible without exception
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The control evaluates whether a critical service retains an unapproved public IP network path.

rule_classifications.name: Azure Firewall threat intelligence not enforcing deny
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Azure Firewall threat intelligence enforces the perimeter across IP addresses, domains, and URLs.

rule_classifications.name: Application Gateway WAF not in Prevention mode
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Application Gateway WAF Prevention mode evaluates and blocks HTTP application requests.

rule_classifications.name: Application Gateway WAF diagnostic logging incomplete
rule_classifications.classification_basis: The control evaluates the diagnostic log categories supported by the Application Gateway SKU; v2 performance telemetry is metric-based.

rule_classifications.name: WAF missing current managed rules or bot protection
rule_classifications.classification_basis: Managed WAF rules inspect HTTP application requests and bot behavior.

rule_classifications.name: Public Application Gateway missing rate limiting
rule_classifications.classification_basis: WAF RateLimitRule evaluates HTTP request volume and application-layer match conditions.
